accepted.s: Who defined capabilities as the substantive freedoms that people have to lead lives they value?
accepted.x: Amartya Sen defined capabilities as the substantive freedoms people possess to lead lives they value.
accepted.tq: Use the person–concept association directly.
accepted.sec: Capability approach - human development vs economic growth

accepted.s: Amartya Sen’s book Development as Freedom was published in which year?
accepted.x: Amartya Sen’s Development as Freedom was published in 1999.
accepted.tq: Recall the publication year from the closely related dates.
accepted.sec: Capability approach - human development vs economic growth

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Economic growth is primarily quantitative and is associated with income.
2. Human development includes both quantitative and qualitative dimensions.
3. Literacy, health and non-discrimination are only instruments of development and not constituents of development.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because literacy, health and non-discrimination are constituents of development as well as possible instruments.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that reverses the distinction between growth and development.
accepted.sec: Capability approach - human development vs economic growth

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Amartya Sen’s approach from Martha Nussbaum’s approach?
o: Nussbaum drew up a list of central capabilities, whereas Sen avoided prescribing a fixed universal list.
Sen prescribed a fixed universal list of capabilities, whereas Nussbaum rejected such a list.
Sen focused only on political freedom, whereas Nussbaum focused only on economic growth.
Both Sen and Nussbaum restricted human development to income growth.
accepted.x: Martha Nussbaum formulated a list of central capabilities, while Amartya Sen deliberately avoided prescribing a fixed universal list.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two closely associated thinkers by their distinctive positions.
accepted.sec: Capability approach - human development vs economic growth

accepted.s: The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index is jointly associated with which of the following organisations?
accepted.x: The Global MPI is produced through the association of the United Nations Development Programme and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct institutional partnership rather than a neighbouring global agency.
accepted.sec: Global MPI and NITI Aayog national MPI - poverty reduction

accepted.s: The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index measures deprivation through how many dimensions and indicators?
accepted.x: The Global MPI comprises 3 dimensions and 10 indicators.
accepted.tq: Separate the number of dimensions from the number of indicators.
accepted.sec: Global MPI and NITI Aayog national MPI - poverty reduction

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct classification of the indicators under the Global MPI?
o: Health—nutrition and child mortality; Education—years of schooling and school attendance; Living standards—six indicators including cooking fuel and sanitation
Health—income and assets; Education—nutrition and housing; Living standards—school attendance only
Health—schooling and sanitation; Education—child mortality and electricity; Living standards—income alone
Health—housing and assets; Education—drinking water and nutrition; Living standards—years of schooling alone
accepted.x: The Global MPI covers nutrition and child mortality under health; years of schooling and school attendance under education; and cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing and assets under living standards.
accepted.tq: Match each indicator to its correct dimension by grouping the sure pairs.
accepted.sec: Global MPI and NITI Aayog national MPI - poverty reduction

accepted.s: India’s value in the Global MPI declined from 0.064 in 2024 to which value in the Global MPI 2025?
accepted.x: India’s Global MPI value was 0.061 in 2025, compared with 0.064 in 2024.
accepted.tq: Track the year-wise numerical change without confusing it with the national MPI value.
accepted.sec: Global MPI and NITI Aayog national MPI - poverty reduction

accepted.s: In addition to the indicators used in the Global MPI, the NITI Aayog National MPI adds which of the following?
o: Life expectancy and per capita income
accepted.x: The NITI Aayog National MPI uses 12 SDG-aligned indicators and adds maternal health and bank account to the Global MPI framework.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the additional national indicators from broader human-development concepts.
accepted.sec: Global MPI and NITI Aayog national MPI - poverty reduction

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the NITI Aayog discussion paper of January 2024:
1. It reported that 24.82 crore people escaped multidimensional poverty between 2013–14 and 2022–23.
2. The multidimensional poverty ratio declined from 29.17 per cent to 11.28 per cent.
3. Uttar Pradesh recorded the largest decline, involving 5.94 crore people.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: 24.82 crore people escaped poverty, the ratio declined by 17.89 percentage points from 29.17% to 11.28%, and Uttar Pradesh recorded the largest fall of 5.94 crore people.
accepted.tq: Verify the complete numerical set rather than relying on one familiar figure.
accepted.sec: Global MPI and NITI Aayog national MPI - poverty reduction

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents India’s National MPI 2023 values for 2019–21?
accepted.x: For 2019–21, the National MPI reported a headcount ratio of 14.96%, intensity of 44.39% and MPI value of 0.066.
accepted.tq: Keep headcount, intensity and composite index figures in their proper columns.
accepted.sec: Global MPI and NITI Aayog national MPI - poverty reduction

accepted.s: According to the World Bank poverty measures stated for India, which change is correctly matched?
o: Poverty at $4.20 per day: 24.82% to 11.28%; extreme poverty at $3 per day: 27.1% to 0.066%
Poverty at $4.20 per day: 23.9% to 57.7%; extreme poverty at $3 per day: 5.3% to 27.1%
Poverty at $4.20 per day: 29.17% to 11.28%; extreme poverty at $3 per day: 14.96% to 6.06%
Poverty at $4.20 per day: 57.7% to 23.9%; extreme poverty at $3 per day: 27.1% to 5.3%
accepted.x: The World Bank figures show a decline from 57.7% to 23.9% at the $4.20-a-day line and from 27.1% to 5.3% at the $3-a-day extreme-poverty line.
accepted.tq: Check both the poverty threshold and the direction of change.
accepted.sec: Global MPI and NITI Aayog national MPI - poverty reduction

accepted.s: Which state is identified with the ‘Kerala Model’ of human development?
accepted.x: Kerala is associated with the Kerala Model, characterised by strong health and education outcomes despite modest income.
accepted.tq: Link the named model with its corresponding state.
accepted.sec: State-level human development - top and bottom states

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about state-level human development:
1. Kerala and Goa have state HDI values above 0.86.
2. Kerala is ranked second on state HDI.
3. Bihar has the lowest state HDI at 0.650 against India’s value of 0.685.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Kerala and Goa are above 0.86, Kerala ranks second, and Bihar records 0.650 against India’s 0.685.
accepted.tq: Combine ranking and figure statements, checking each independently.
accepted.sec: State-level human development - top and bottom states

accepted.s: Which of the following states are also identified as having low human development along with Bihar?
accepted.x: Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh are also identified among the states with low human development.
accepted.tq: Select the associated pair from the same state-level classification.
accepted.sec: State-level human development - top and bottom states

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (State) 
A. Assam
B. West Bengal
C. Kerala
D. Bihar
List-II (State HDI/MPI fact)
1. HDI 0.719
2. HDI 0.699 and rank 24 of 29
3. MPI 0.002
4. MPI 0.16
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
accepted.x: Assam is 24th of 29 with an HDI of 0.699; West Bengal has 0.719; Kerala has the lowest MPI of 0.002; and Bihar has the highest MPI of 0.16.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive MPI extremes and then complete the HDI pairs.
accepted.sec: State-level human development - top and bottom states

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the position in the SDG India Index 2023–24?
o: Kerala and Uttarakhand jointly top the index with 79, while Bihar is at the bottom with 57.
Bihar tops with 79, while Kerala is at the bottom with 57.
Kerala tops with 57, while Bihar and Uttarakhand jointly rank at 79.
Uttarakhand ranks 57, while Kerala and Bihar jointly score 79.
accepted.x: Kerala and Uttarakhand jointly occupy the top position with a score of 79, whereas Bihar is at the bottom with 57.
accepted.tq: Compare the top and bottom values and avoid reversing the ranking.
accepted.sec: State-level human development - top and bottom states

accepted.s: The state-level figures in which the India average is 0.732 for 2023 should NOT be confused with which figure?
o: West Bengal’s state HDI value of 0.719
accepted.x: The sub-national series gives an India average of 0.732 for 2023, whereas the UNDP figure stated for India is 0.685.
accepted.tq: Separate figures from different series before comparing state and national values.
accepted.sec: State-level human development - top and bottom states

accepted.s: A fall in the Multidimensional Poverty Index from 0.053 in 2015–16 to 0.025 in 2019–21 represents what change for Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh’s MPI fell by 50%, from 0.053 to 0.025 during the stated period.
accepted.tq: Calculate the percentage change from the two stated index values.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Andhra Pradesh’s multidimensional poverty position?
o: Its headcount ratio was 2.42%, while Bihar had the lowest district ratio in Andhra Pradesh.
Its headcount ratio was 14.96%, twice the national figure, and West Godavari had the highest ratio at 24.82%.
Its headcount ratio was 6.06%, under half the national 14.96%, placing it ninth best; West Godavari had the lowest ratio at 2.42%.
Its headcount ratio was 23.9%, placing it last among the States.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded a headcount ratio of 6.06%, less than half the national 14.96%, ranked ninth best, and West Godavari recorded the lowest ratio at 2.42%.
accepted.tq: Use the comparison phrase ‘under half’ and identify the associated district figure.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: A UNDP simulation of April 2026 estimated that the West Asia war could have which effect on India’s human development and poverty?
o: It could reduce HDI progress by 3–12 years and raise poverty to 42.2%.
It could increase HDI progress by 0.03–0.12 years and reduce poverty to 23.9%.
It could leave HDI progress unchanged and raise poverty from 14.96% to 24.82%.
It could reduce HDI progress by 0.03–0.12 years and raise poverty from 23.9% to 24.2%.
accepted.x: The simulation estimated a possible loss of 0.03–0.12 years of HDI progress and an increase in poverty from 23.9% to 24.2%.
accepted.tq: Apply the stated cause-and-effect relationship while preserving the range and percentages.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: India sources more than what proportion of its crude oil from West Asia, as stated in the context of the possible regional-war impact?
accepted.x: India sources over 40% of its crude oil from West Asia.
accepted.tq: Recall the approximate threshold rather than substituting a nearby share.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a criticism of the Human Development Index?
o: It completely excludes health and education
It ignores gender and political freedom
accepted.x: The HDI includes health and education dimensions. Its stated criticisms concern the inadequate treatment of inequality, sustainability, gender and political freedom, leading to the development of companion indices.
accepted.tq: Find the option that contradicts the basic content of the index rather than its limitations.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: According to the World Inequality Database figure stated for 2023–24, the income of the top 10 per cent is approximately how many times that of the bottom 10 per cent?
accepted.x: The top 10% are reported to earn approximately 13 times the income of the bottom 10%.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the reported inequality multiple from rounded neighbouring values.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly identifies the first Human Development Report and the first National Human Development Report of India?
accepted.x: The first Human Development Report was published in 1990, while India’s first National Human Development Report was published in 2001.
accepted.tq: Arrange the two landmark reports by their publication years.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
